To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

immersion in sodium per borate solution and microwave disinfection adversely affected the surface roughness of some denture base and relining materials, and that the surface roughness was not significantly changed by disinfection with sodium per borate or microwave irradiation in most denture base and denture reline materials tested.

immersion in sodium peroxoborate solution for 1 minute daily and microwave disinfection (650 W for 6 minutes) did not affect surface roughness of Lucitone 550 denture base resin, Tokuyama ReBase II and Dentusil resilient reline materials.
microwave disinfection and immersion in sodium per borate adversely affected the roughness of some reline materials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of disinfection by microwave irradiation or immersion in sodium peraborate on the surface roughness of 6 materials used for reline and relining of complete dentures.
the surface roughness of 6 different materials used for denture base and denture reline, which were submitted to disinfection by immersion and microwave irradiation.
the effect of chemical disinfection and microwave irradiation in the surface roughness of dentures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
disinfection of the denture base and relining materials by immersion in water or sodium perborate or microwave disinfection does not significantly alter the surface roughness of the materials tested.
the surface roughness of dentures and relining materials can be altered by the use of chemical disinfection or by microwave irradiation.
disinfection by immersion or microwave irradiation may adversely affect the roughness of dentures and reline materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the roughness of materials Ufi Gel Hard and New Trulinner were adversely affected by microwave irradiation, immersion in water and immersion in sodium per borate solution, whereas microwave irradiation caused severe alterations on Trusoft surface.
disinfection of reline materials should be done with caution, and that immersion in sodium peraborate solution is preferable to microwave irradiation.
microwave irradiation and immersion in sodium per borate solution are effective disinfecting techniques for the hard chairside rebase materials and denture base resin Lucitone 550.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface roughness of the materials evaluated was not affected by immersion in sodium peroxyhydrate solution or microwave irradiation, except for Ufi Gel hard, New Trulinen and Trusoft.
the surface of denture base resins and reline materials can be altered by chemical disinfection and microwave irradiation, with the resilient liner material Trusoft being most affected.
the use of microwave irradiation for disinfecting denture base and chairside reline materials is not recommended.
